"""FastAPI application factory, CORS, and route mounting."""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

from agentforge.api.routes_health import router as health_router
from agentforge.api.routes_tasks import router as tasks_router
from agentforge.api.routes_events import router as events_router
from agentforge.api.routes_projects import router as projects_router
from agentforge.api.routes_artifacts import router as artifacts_router
from agentforge.api.routes_configuration import router as configuration_router
from agentforge.auth.routes import router as auth_router
from agentforge.auth.session import SessionStore
from agentforge.database.engine import create_db_engine
from agentforge.settings import Settings, get_settings


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    settings: Settings = app.state.settings
    owns_engine = not hasattr(app.state, "engine")
    if owns_engine:
        app.state.engine = create_db_engine(settings.database_url)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        if owns_engine:
            app.state.engine.dispose()


def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    """Build the ASGI app. Uvicorn loads `agentforge.main:app`."""
    resolved = settings or get_settings()
    app = FastAPI(
        title="AgentForge AI API",
        version="0.1.0",
        description="HTTP API for the AgentForge AI workspace.",
        lifespan=lifespan,
        openapi_tags=[
            {
                "name": "health",
                "description": "Liveness and readiness probes.",
            }
        ],
    )
    app.state.settings = resolved
    app.state.auth_sessions = SessionStore()
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=resolved.allowed_origins,
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "OPTIONS"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )
    app.include_router(health_router)
    app.include_router(auth_router)
    app.include_router(projects_router)
    app.include_router(tasks_router)
    app.include_router(events_router)
    app.include_router(artifacts_router)
    app.include_router(configuration_router)
    @app.middleware("http")
    async def private_response_headers(request, call_next):
        response = await call_next(request)
        if request.url.path.startswith("/api/v1/") and not request.url.path.startswith("/api/v1/health/"):
            response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
            response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
        return response
    return app


app = create_app()
"""Immutable research persistence with fresh task/project ownership on every read."""

from collections.abc import Callable
import hashlib
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from agentforge.database.models import AgentRun, Project, Task
from agentforge.database.research_models import ResearchArtifact, ResearchEvidence, ResearchSource
from agentforge.subagents.scope import ScopeDenied, TaskContext


def _uuid(value: str | UUID) -> UUID:
    try:
        parsed = UUID(str(value))
        if str(parsed) != str(value):
            raise ValueError("noncanonical reference")
        return parsed
    except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
        raise ScopeDenied("invalid research reference") from None


class ResearchRepository:
    def __init__(self, session_factory: Callable[[], Session]) -> None:
        self.session_factory = session_factory

    @staticmethod
    def _owned(session: Session, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> Task:
        task = session.scalar(select(Task).join(Project, Project.id == Task.project_id).where(
            Task.id == task_id, Task.project_id == project_id, Task.created_by == owner_id,
            Project.owner_id == owner_id))
        if task is None:
            raise ScopeDenied("research task ownership is not authorized")
        return task

    @staticmethod
    def _scope(ctx: TaskContext) -> dict[str, UUID]:
        return {"task_id": ctx.task_id, "owner_id": ctx.user_id, "project_id": ctx.project_id}

    @staticmethod
    def _writable(task: Task) -> None:
        if task.cancel_requested_at is not None or task.status in {"COMPLETED", "PARTIAL", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"}:
            raise ScopeDenied("research task no longer accepts new evidence")

    @staticmethod
    def _source(row: ResearchSource, *, full: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        value = {"id": str(row.id), "task_id": str(row.task_id), "url": row.url,
                 "title": row.title, "excerpt": row.content[:2000], "content_sha256": row.content_sha256,
                 "source_type": row.source_type, "fetch_status": row.fetch_status,
                 "retrieved_at": row.retrieved_at.isoformat(), "error_code": row.error_code}
        if full:
            value["content"] = row.content
        return value

    @staticmethod
    def _preview_columns() -> tuple:
        return (ResearchSource.id, ResearchSource.task_id, ResearchSource.url,
                ResearchSource.title, func.substr(ResearchSource.content, 1, 2000).label("excerpt"),
                ResearchSource.content_sha256, ResearchSource.source_type,
                ResearchSource.fetch_status, ResearchSource.retrieved_at, ResearchSource.error_code)

    @staticmethod
    def _source_preview(row) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"id": str(row["id"]), "task_id": str(row["task_id"]), "url": row["url"],
                "title": row["title"], "excerpt": row["excerpt"],
                "content_sha256": row["content_sha256"], "source_type": row["source_type"],
                "fetch_status": row["fetch_status"], "retrieved_at": row["retrieved_at"].isoformat(),
                "error_code": row["error_code"]}

    @staticmethod
    def _artifact(row: ResearchArtifact, *, internal: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        value = {"id": str(row.id), "task_id": str(row.task_id), "kind": row.kind,
                 "filename": row.filename, "mime_type": row.mime_type, "byte_size": row.byte_size,
                 "sha256": row.sha256, "created_at": row.created_at.isoformat()}
        if internal:
            value["storage_key"] = row.storage_key
            value["metadata"] = row.metadata_json
        return value

    def add_source(self, ctx: TaskContext, *, run_id: UUID, operation_key: str, ordinal: int,
                   url: str, title: str, content: str, source_type: str,
                   fetch_status: str, error_code: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if len(content.encode()) > 2_000_000 or len(url) > 2048 or len(title) > 1000:
            raise ValueError("research_source_size_limit")
        with self.session_factory() as session, session.begin():
            self._writable(self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx)))
            run = session.scalar(select(AgentRun.id).where(AgentRun.id == run_id, AgentRun.task_id == ctx.task_id))
            if run is None:
                raise ScopeDenied("research run is outside the task")
            existing = session.scalar(select(ResearchSource).where(ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id,
                ResearchSource.operation_key == operation_key, ResearchSource.ordinal == ordinal))
            if existing is not None:
                if (existing.agent_run_id != run_id or existing.url != url or existing.title != title or
                    existing.content != content or existing.source_type != source_type or
                    existing.fetch_status != fetch_status or existing.error_code != error_code):
                    raise ScopeDenied("immutable source operation does not match its original inputs")
                return self._source(existing)
            row = ResearchSource(id=uuid4(), task_id=ctx.task_id, agent_run_id=run_id,
                operation_key=operation_key, ordinal=ordinal, url=url, title=title,
                content=content, content_sha256=hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest(),
                source_type=source_type, fetch_status=fetch_status, error_code=error_code)
            session.add(row)
            session.flush()
            # Every source ID is independently acceptable as a source reference;
            # this evidence record records what retrieval actually establishes.
            session.add(ResearchEvidence(id=uuid4(), task_id=ctx.task_id, source_id=row.id,
                kind="source_retrieval", validation_state=fetch_status,
                evidence_json={"content_sha256": row.content_sha256, "fetch_status": fetch_status}))
            return self._source(row)

    def list_sources(self, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, task_id=task_id, owner_id=owner_id, project_id=project_id)
            rows = session.execute(select(*self._preview_columns()).where(
                ResearchSource.task_id == task_id).order_by(ResearchSource.retrieved_at, ResearchSource.id).limit(1000)).mappings()
            return [self._source_preview(row) for row in rows]

    def read_source(self, source_id: str, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, task_id=task_id, owner_id=owner_id, project_id=project_id)
            row = session.scalar(select(ResearchSource).where(ResearchSource.id == _uuid(source_id),
                                                            ResearchSource.task_id == task_id))
            if row is None:
                raise ScopeDenied("source reference is outside the task")
            return self._source(row, full=True)

    def sources_for_url(self, ctx: TaskContext, url: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))
            rows = session.execute(select(*self._preview_columns()).where(
                ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id, ResearchSource.url == url,
                ResearchSource.fetch_status.in_(("SEARCH_ONLY", "FETCHED"))).order_by(ResearchSource.retrieved_at).limit(1000)).mappings()
            return [self._source_preview(row) for row in rows]

    def verify_references(self, ctx: TaskContext, *, evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...], artifact_ids: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))
            evidence = {_uuid(value) for value in evidence_ids}
            artifacts = {_uuid(value) for value in artifact_ids}
            found = set(session.scalars(select(ResearchSource.id).where(
                ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id, ResearchSource.id.in_(evidence))))
            found.update(session.scalars(select(ResearchEvidence.id).where(
                ResearchEvidence.task_id == ctx.task_id, ResearchEvidence.id.in_(evidence))))
            found_artifacts = set(session.scalars(select(ResearchArtifact.id).where(
                ResearchArtifact.task_id == ctx.task_id, ResearchArtifact.id.in_(artifacts))))
            if found != evidence or found_artifacts != artifacts:
                raise ScopeDenied("research reference is outside the task")

    def load_reference(self, ctx: TaskContext, reference: str) -> str:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))
            source = session.scalar(select(ResearchSource).where(ResearchSource.id == _uuid(reference),
                                                                ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id))
            if source is not None:
                preview = source.content.encode("utf-8")[:4000].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
                return f"UNTRUSTED SOURCE {source.id}\nURL: {source.url}\nStatus: {source.fetch_status}\n{preview}"
            evidence = session.scalar(select(ResearchEvidence).where(ResearchEvidence.id == _uuid(reference),
                                                                    ResearchEvidence.task_id == ctx.task_id))
            if evidence is not None and evidence.source_id is not None:
                source = session.scalar(select(ResearchSource).where(ResearchSource.id == evidence.source_id,
                                                                    ResearchSource.task_id == ctx.task_id))
                if source is not None:
                    preview = source.content.encode("utf-8")[:4000].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
                    return f"UNTRUSTED EVIDENCE {evidence.id}\nSource: {source.id}\nStatus: {source.fetch_status}\n{preview}"
            raise ScopeDenied("context reference is not a readable task source")

    def research_results(self, ctx: TaskContext) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))
            rows = session.scalars(select(AgentRun).where(AgentRun.task_id == ctx.task_id,
                AgentRun.result_json.is_not(None)).order_by(AgentRun.started_at, AgentRun.id).limit(100))
            return [row.result_json for row in rows if row.result_json and
                    row.definition_snapshot.get("output_schema_id") == "research_result_v1"]

    def goal(self, ctx: TaskContext) -> str:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            return self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx)).goal

    def list_artifacts(self, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, task_id=task_id, owner_id=owner_id, project_id=project_id)
            return [self._artifact(row) for row in session.scalars(select(ResearchArtifact).where(
                ResearchArtifact.task_id == task_id).order_by(ResearchArtifact.created_at, ResearchArtifact.id).limit(100))]

    def get_artifact(self, artifact_id: str, *, task_id: UUID, owner_id: UUID, project_id: UUID) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, task_id=task_id, owner_id=owner_id, project_id=project_id)
            row = session.scalar(select(ResearchArtifact).where(ResearchArtifact.id == _uuid(artifact_id),
                                                                ResearchArtifact.task_id == task_id))
            if row is None:
                raise ScopeDenied("artifact reference is outside the task")
            return self._artifact(row, internal=True)

    def artifact_for_operation(self, ctx: TaskContext, operation_key: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        with self.session_factory() as session:
            self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx))
            row = session.scalar(select(ResearchArtifact).where(ResearchArtifact.task_id == ctx.task_id,
                ResearchArtifact.operation_key == operation_key))
            return self._artifact(row, internal=True) if row else None

    def add_artifact(self, ctx: TaskContext, *, artifact_id: UUID, operation_key: str,
                     storage_key: str, sha256: str, byte_size: int, metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if not storage_key.startswith(f"{ctx.task_id}/"):
            raise ScopeDenied("artifact storage key is outside the task")
        with self.session_factory() as session, session.begin():
            self._writable(self._owned(session, **self._scope(ctx)))
            row = ResearchArtifact(id=artifact_id, task_id=ctx.task_id, operation_key=operation_key,
                kind="research_report", filename="research-report.md", mime_type="text/markdown; charset=utf-8",
                storage_key=storage_key, sha256=sha256, byte_size=byte_size, metadata_json=metadata)
            session.add(row)
            session.flush()
            return self._artifact(row, internal=True)
"use client";

import Link from "next/link";
import { useEffect, useState, type FormEvent } from "react";
import { ArrowRight, Plus, RefreshCw } from "lucide-react";

import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Badge } from "@/components/ui/badge";
import { inputClass } from "@/components/session-boundary";
import { api, formatDate, message, statusLabel, type Project, type Task } from "@/lib/task-api";

type Configuration = {
  research_configured: boolean;
  missing_settings: string[];
  tracing_configured: boolean;
  qualification: string;
};

export function TaskWorkspace() {
  const [projects, setProjects] = useState<Project[]>([]);
  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState<Task[]>([]);
  const [config, setConfig] = useState<Configuration | null>(null);
  const [projectId, setProjectId] = useState("");
  const [goal, setGoal] = useState("");
  const [cost, setCost] = useState("0.50");
  const [seconds, setSeconds] = useState("300");
  const [hosts, setHosts] = useState("");
  const [projectName, setProjectName] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState("");
  const [submitError, setSubmitError] = useState("");
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const [creatingProject, setCreatingProject] = useState(false);
  const [refresh, setRefresh] = useState(0);
  const [offset, setOffset] = useState(0);
  const [createdTask, setCreatedTask] = useState<Task | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    let inFlight = false;
    async function load() {
      if (inFlight) return;
      inFlight = true;
      try {
        const [nextProjects, nextTasks, nextConfig] = await Promise.all([
          api<Project[]>("/projects", { signal: controller.signal }),
          api<Task[]>(`/tasks?limit=20&offset=${offset}`, { signal: controller.signal }),
          api<Configuration>("/configuration", { signal: controller.signal }),
        ]);
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) {
          setProjects(nextProjects);
          setProjectId((current) => nextProjects.some((project) => project.id === current) ? current : nextProjects[0]?.id ?? "");
          setTasks(nextTasks);
          setConfig(nextConfig);
          setError("");
        }
      } catch (error) {
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setError(message(error));
      } finally {
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) setLoading(false);
        inFlight = false;
      }
    }
    void load();
    const timer = window.setInterval(() => { void load(); }, 10000);
    return () => { controller.abort(); window.clearInterval(timer); };
  }, [refresh, offset]);

  async function submit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault();
    setSubmitError("");
    const numericCost = Number(cost);
    const numericSeconds = Number(seconds);
    const allowedHosts = hosts.split(/[\s,]+/).map((host) => host.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean);
    if (!projectId || goal.trim().length < 20 || goal.trim().length > 8000 || !Number.isFinite(numericCost) || numericCost <= 0 || numericCost > 5 || !Number.isInteger(numericSeconds) || numericSeconds < 30 || numericSeconds > 1200 || allowedHosts.length > 20) {
      setSubmitError("Choose a project, write at least 20 characters, and keep the limits within the ranges shown.");
      return;
    }
    setSubmitting(true);
    try {
      const task = await api<Task>("/tasks", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({
        project_id: projectId, goal: goal.trim(), max_cost_usd: cost,
        max_wall_time_sec: numericSeconds, allowed_web_hosts: allowedHosts,
      }) });
      // Show a durable receipt before navigation; a failed navigation must never
      // encourage an accidental second paid task submission.
      setCreatedTask(task);
      setGoal("");
      setOffset(0);
      setRefresh((value) => value + 1);
    } catch (error) { setSubmitError(message(error)); }
    finally { setSubmitting(false); }
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid items-start gap-12 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1.05fr)_minmax(0,1fr)] lg:gap-16">
      <section aria-labelledby="composer-title" className="min-w-0 space-y-7">
        <div className="space-y-3">
          <h1 id="composer-title" className="text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight">What would you like to research?</h1>
          <p className="max-w-prose text-sm leading-relaxed text-muted-foreground">Give your agents a clear question and a budget. Follow the plan, review the sources, and download the final report.</p>
        </div>
        {loading ? <div aria-label="Loading workspace" className="space-y-4"><div className="h-10 rounded-lg bg-muted" /><div className="h-44 rounded-lg bg-muted" /></div> : null}
        {error ? <div role="alert" className="space-y-3"><p className="text-sm text-destructive">{error}</p><Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setRefresh((value) => value + 1)}>Retry</Button></div> : null}
        {config && !config.research_configured ? (
          <div className="rounded-xl border bg-muted/30 p-4 text-sm leading-relaxed">
            <p className="font-medium">Research setup is incomplete</p>
            <p className="mt-1 text-muted-foreground">Configure the following API settings, restart the API and worker, then refresh this page:</p>
            <ul className="mt-3 list-inside list-disc break-words text-xs leading-6">{config.missing_settings.map((name) => <li key={name}><code>{name}</code></li>)}</ul>
          </div>
        ) : null}

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
# New visual work

Use this flow for a new surface or a replacement visual identity. PRODUCT.md owns product truth. DESIGN.md owns durable visual decisions. A surface brief keeps strategy that belongs to one route or artifact. Complete [init.md](init.md) first when PRODUCT.md is missing; a missing DESIGN.md does not route back to init.

## 1. Decide what is already true

Read DESIGN.md, representative code, tokens, components, and assets.

- **Redesign:** preserve product truth, content, function, constraints, and explicit brand commitments; replace the old visual world rather than polishing it. The old look is evidence of what the subject is, not authority over what it becomes.
- **Established world:** inherit it. A missing DESIGN.md does not erase a coherent identity already in code; document that identity instead of inventing a replacement.
- **Incomplete brand:** preserve confirmed assets and recognizable traits, then expand the system with the user for this surface.
- **No visual authority:** create a new world with the user.

A section, component, feature, or state inside an established surface inherits that surface. Never turn a local addition into a new identity exercise.

## 2. Ask what will change the work

Ask one round of two or three related questions through the structured question tool when available. Skip settled facts; a precise request may need only a compact confirmation.

- **Persuade:** who must act, what they should believe, which real proof, content, or assets earn that belief.
- **Operate:** the task, information, important states, frequency, constraints.
- **Read:** the reader's question, source material, structure, wayfinding.
- **Experience:** what leads, how exploration unfolds, which interaction or transition matters.

Across modes, ask what success looks like, what must remain untouched, and what would make a polished result feel wrong. Never ask for CSS values or canned aesthetic lanes.

## 3. Choose the right amount of invention

### Extend an existing surface

Inherit its world and composition. Resolve only the new purpose, content, hierarchy, states, interaction, and how the addition joins the surrounding experience. No concept tournament, and no DESIGN.md change unless the user approves a durable system change.

### Create a whole surface inside an established world

Keep the visual system fixed. Derive five to seven materially different structures from the content, task, and user behavior, ordered by resonance. For a genuinely open whole page, screen, or flow, run:

`node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope surface --mode <mode>`

The script deals three of your structures; the dice pick which three reach the user, breaking the ranking rut while the user keeps a real choice. Present them on the decision page as full cards of equal salience, the dealt lead under kicker THE ROLL, with steer and re-roll; the user locks one. No canon card and no pick card at surface scope: the world is settled, so every card visualizes composition, not identity. With image generation and a comp-led default (`.impeccable/config.json`; the build-path paragraph below), each card declares a `comp` under `.impeccable/mocks/decision/`, generated after serving, in reading order, under [visualize.md](visualize.md)'s comp discipline. Anchor each comp on the established identity: pass a screenshot of a representative existing page as a reference image (the harness image tool's input image, or `generate-image.mjs --ref`) with a prompt that leads with the new surface's structure and names DESIGN.md's palette, type, and component character; prose paraphrases of a design system drift, pixel references do not. Without image generation, or under a code-led default, each card carries a `wireframe` schematic (`serve-question.mjs --schema`) the page draws itself. Locking a card is the approval and sets the build path: a locked comp builds comp-led with that comp as the approved comp, discharging [visualize.md](visualize.md)'s three-option round with no second approval point; a locked wireframe builds code-led, its ambition carried by the direction contract. Never run the script for a local extension or a precisely specified narrow request; shape those directly.

### Create or replace the visual world

1. Name the product's unique mechanism in one sentence, the audience's real scene, its cultural home, and what this first surface must prove. Note the page this category always ships and its predictable opposite; both are the rut, kept out of the seven-candidate list. A brief that paints its own picture, a product name, a titled artifact, a governing metaphor, adds its literal reading to the rut: spend at most one candidate on it and derive the rest from elsewhere in the audience's world.
2. From that cultural world, list seven concrete visual systems, artifacts, places, or rituals the audience knows by heart, each with one line on why it resonates and can carry the mechanism, ordered by resonance. The audience's world includes its graphic and screen traditions, not only its physical objects: the notation, publications, identity programs, data graphics, and interfaces it reads daily. A nameable abstract system (a school of poster, a documentation standard) is as concrete a candidate as any artifact. What would this thing look like as a physical object; what did its world look like before the web? Near-duplicates count once. When more than three of the seven share one material family, the derivation stopped at the subject's most obvious artifact; dig until the list spans at least three families.
3. Turn that material into complete directions: each joins a reusable visual world to a concrete first-surface experience.
4. Run `node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope direction --mode <mode>` and follow what it prints. No substitute, no skip: on a new or replacement world, writing artifact code before this script has run and its assignment is acknowledged is a contract violation, whatever the harness, the model, or the time pressure; the roll is what keeps every run from converging on the category default. The script assigns the direction to build and deals catalog challengers. Fuse each challenger before judging it: the challenger supplies the form and its system grammar, the product supplies every fact, clarity wins conflicts. Weigh fused challengers against the assigned direction on exactly two axes, audience identification and product clarity. Losing to strong grounded material is a valid outcome; beating a thin or tool-monoculture list is the point. Close with a verdict per challenger, decided before any borrowing: wins (beats the assigned direction on both axes; becomes the build candidate), competitive (holds one axis; stays a full alternate), or declined (loses both). A declined challenger is not spent: name the one discipline of its system the assigned direction lacks, and raise the assigned direction to match before presenting it. A donation transfers ambition and system discipline (a palette's total commitment, a grid's density courage, a form's structural honesty), never the challenger's clothes; a lifted motif is a costume note, not a raise, and one world owns the page. Write each raise into the presented direction as its own line, named for its donor; a raise nobody can read did not happen.
5. Present one direction, fully committed and already raised by the hand it beat, raises visible as named lines: world, first viewport, visitor path, signature interaction, cross-surface reach, honest risk. The verdict informs the user's choice, never pre-empts it; the demoted row is the hand's proof of judgment. A hand holds at most three full-card challengers: when the roll deals more, the three strongest join and the rest wait in the re-roll pool, noted in one line; dropping a challenger from the hand itself takes a named product-truth failure, disclosed. Add one card for your own top-ranked grounded candidate when it is not the assigned direction, kicker IMPECCABLE’S PICK, same anatomy as every card, with an honest risk line naming its familiarity when true: the strongest grounded direction is often where most runs in this category land, and the user deciding that trade is the point of showing it. Familiar and effective is a legitimate destination, not a failure of nerve; the pick card and the standing exit serve it at two depths. One pick card, never two, never a ranked list: a lineup of your candidates hands selection back to a taste function and invites the safest card. The pick never takes the lead position; when the dice assign your top candidate there is no pick card, and the assigned card notes it topped your list. Add re-roll with an optional one-line steer, in three registers: plain (a fresh hand, same spread), safer (your remaining conventional grounded candidates plus the canon against named competitors), bolder (foreign forms only, at full commitment). The register is the user's steering on the familiar-to-bold axis, never yours to pre-select; when the answer carries one, re-run the seed with `--register <value>` and the next `--reroll` round, and follow what it prints. A user saying "bolder" or "safer" while a direction round is open means these registers, never the bolder or harden commands. The two channels share this structure and differ only in richness: cards and boards on the decision page, names and one-liners through the structured tool, whose option list carries the assigned direction, the pick, the winning and competitive challengers, and the standing exit last; declined challengers fold into the assigned option's description as their kept lines, so the raise survives the text channel.

The standing exit: every direction round offers one quiet, permanent alternative, the category standard, played straight. It is the user's door, never yours: never recommend it, never weigh it against the roll, never let it soften the dealt directions; the counterweights bind the unchosen default, not the chosen one. When the user takes it (the canon action, a safer-steer, or plain words asking for the familiar or competitor-like path), convention becomes the commitment: ask once for two or three products this should sit alongside, make their craft level the bar, and execute the canon at full fidelity, without irony or smuggled quirk. Record a standing preference as a brand commitment in PRODUCT.md. Re-roll eliminates every direction already shown, grounded and challenger alike; after two consecutive re-rolls, ask what quality is missing. Re-roll on your own only on named factual grounds, when the assigned direction cannot carry the product's truth or task; taste is never grounds. The user may re-roll freely, and a user- or brief-pinned direction beats the roll, always. Resolve collisions field by field: preserve every user- or brief-pinned constraint. In dimensions the brief leaves open, the assignment still binds through its topology, controls, state vocabulary, and ritual; when only its materials conflict with a pinned visual direction or PRODUCT.md brand commitment, translate that material expression and name the translation in the presented direction. A look mismatch is not grounds to re-roll. A degraded roll with no challengers still uses the page, as a single text-only card with re-roll. Run `node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/serve-question.mjs --start --payload <file>` (`--schema` first for the payload shape). It daemonizes, prints the page URL and a key, and exits; open that URL for the user, in-app browser first, then the system opener, then showing the URL. Where the harness sandboxes its shell, start the page through the least-sandboxed command path it offers: a sandboxed shell cannot bind the board's port, and the first-attempt failure costs a retry every session. With parallel subagents, fan out one agent per card: each spawn is the shipped asset producer with a single-comp packet, that card's fields, PRODUCT.md, the shared frame, and the card's declared path, up to four in flight. Regenerate inline any slot still empty when its agent returns; drop without ceremony any slot still empty when the user answers. No other supervision is owed. Unchosen comps stay in `.impeccable/mocks/decision/` as the round's spent hand; they carry no approval and imply none. The execution contract, comp-led or code-led, is a workflow preference, not a per-surface decision; no round asks it. The recorded default rides every round and the page's toggle handles the exception. Read the default from `.impeccable/config.json` (`buildPath`), the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json` winning where one machine differs from the team's committed value; with neither, comp-led is the default whenever image generation exists. Every direction the roll can land on must already be viable: every relationship and claim it visualizes true, a real palette and component family, a distinctive composition with one product-specific experience, workable at full-surface scale within the available assets, tools, and performance budget. Conversion lives inside the form's own vocabulary: a hook that lands in one line, a visible primary action, a legible reading order. A committed form that hides the offer or the action has not finished translating. For **Operate**, expression may never obscure the task, state, or familiar affordance. For **Read**, comprehension and wayfinding remain intact. For **Experience**, the work itself leads from the first viewport.

## 4. Commit the world

Pick a color strategy before picking colors: Restrained (neutrals plus one accent; the default when the visitor came to operate or read), Committed (one saturated color carries 30-60% of the surface), Full palette (3-4 named roles), or Drenched (the surface IS the color). Persuade and Experience surfaces have permission for the bolder strategies; take them when the brief allows. Color commits at page scale: fields that own whole regions, not accents scattered over a neutral ground. Dark or light is never a default: write one sentence of physical scene (who uses this, where, under what light) and let it force the answer.

Choose faces like objects from the subject's world, in the mode's register. Operate and Read surfaces are well served by system stacks and workhorse UI faces; Persuade and Experience surfaces want faces with a point of view, and these training-data defaults mean you stopped looking: Fraunces, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Lora, Crimson, Newsreader, Syne, Space Grotesk, Space Mono, IBM Plex, Inter-as-display, DM Sans, DM Serif, Outfit, Plus Jakarta Sans, Instrument Sans. Naming one of these faces anyway requires a reason no other face could satisfy, and a subject association is never that reason: books wanting a serif, bookshops wanting hand-lettering, and tech wanting a mono are the associations the list exists to break.

Calibration: AI-generated interfaces cluster around a few looks regardless of subject: warm cream ground, high-contrast serif display, and a terracotta or signal-red accent; near-black with one neon accent and glowing edges; broadsheet-editorial hairlines, italic display serif, and small tracked mono labels. All are legitimate when the brief calls for them. Where the brief leaves the aesthetic free, landing in one means the self-check failed: if someone could guess your aesthetic from the category alone, or from category-plus-avoidance, rework until neither answer is obvious. Energy is not the enemy of trust: a brief's negative constraints (no gamification, no hype) rule out those devices, not exuberance, and adjectives describing the product's behavior (quiet support, calm coaching) do not dictate the surface's energy. A bookish, warm, or child-facing subject does not soften the calibration: book cloth, thread, jackets, endpapers, and shelf ephemera span the whole saturated spectrum, and cream paper is the smallest corner of that world; landing on cream plus serif for a book subject is the default wearing the subject's clothes. A brief-pinned world pins the world, not its softest rendition: the pinned world's full material range stays in play, and a rendition matching what any model ships for that world failed the self-check at execution rather than selection.

## 5. Record the decision

Before code, record the chosen direction as a development-only contract under `## Direction contract` in the relevant surface brief. A direction contract is durable route or artifact strategy, so create or update the brief even when no other surface strategy needs persistence. Keep the contract to six short blocks and 150 words at most. THESIS: the one idea this surface owns and the category-default arrangement it refuses. OWN-WORLD: the palette and component language, specific enough to be recognizable with all content removed. STORY: what the visitor understands, believes, and does. FIRST VIEWPORT: the exact composition, what is where and at what scale, and where the primary action sits. FORM: the chosen form, its position on your ordered list, and the seed key the script printed. Close with one more line, FINISH: the run's exit condition, verbatim "unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance". The surface brief is the reminder later agents reload across edits and sessions: a page that looks complete with the FINISH line undischarged is not done, it is abandoned at the finish line. If a block reads like a mood, the direction is not decided yet; the finishing review audits the render against this contract.

Never copy the direction contract into implementation source or any browser-delivered artifact. This includes HTML or framework comments, hidden DOM, `<template>` elements, `data-*` attributes, rendered JSX or TSX output, serialized props or state, React Server Component payloads, client bundles, metadata or JSON-LD, accessibility-only text, and files served beside the artifact. A compiler or optimizer removing development metadata is not a safety boundary. Reviewers and documenters receive the contract from the surface brief.

On a new or replacement world, DESIGN.md is written at finish, from the built world, by the shipped documenter (section 7); a rulebook written before the build gets defended against reality instead of describing it, and hands the design-system detector an unstable target. A new world shipped with no DESIGN.md is still an incomplete run. An ordinary extension does not rewrite DESIGN.md.

Read the existing surface brief before updating it:

`node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/surface-brief.mjs read <primary-target>`

`node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/surface-brief.mjs write <primary-target> <body-file> [related-target ...]`

After writing, read the brief once more and verify that all six contract blocks and the seed key are present before building.

Keep the brief small: scope and visitor mode; audience, job, action/task, proof/content, and constraints; chosen direction and memorable moment; unresolved decisions. Do not copy global product truth or DESIGN.md tokens into it.

On a comp-led build, whenever any image generation is available (a harness-native tool or the API fallback context.mjs reports), the locked direction is visualized before it is built, never skipped: load [visualize.md](visualize.md) and follow it, three compositional options put before the user for approval, the chosen card's decision comp plus two variations. This step is proven to produce the most compositional and ambitious work. On a code-led build the comp round is skipped by contract, never by drift: the ambition it would have carried lives in the direction contract's FIRST VIEWPORT block and named signature interaction, and the finish reviewer audits those promises in behavior.

For `shape`, return the selected direction to [shape.md](shape.md) and stop before persistence or implementation.

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
# New visual work

Use this flow for a new surface or a replacement visual identity. PRODUCT.md owns product truth. DESIGN.md owns durable visual decisions. A surface brief keeps strategy that belongs to one route or artifact. Complete [init.md](init.md) first when PRODUCT.md is missing; a missing DESIGN.md does not route back to init.

## 1. Decide what is already true

Read DESIGN.md, representative code, tokens, components, and assets.

- **Redesign:** preserve product truth, content, function, constraints, and explicit brand commitments; replace the old visual world rather than polishing it. The old look is evidence of what the subject is, not authority over what it becomes.
- **Established world:** inherit it. A missing DESIGN.md does not erase a coherent identity already in code; document that identity instead of inventing a replacement.
- **Incomplete brand:** preserve confirmed assets and recognizable traits, then expand the system with the user for this surface.
- **No visual authority:** create a new world with the user.

A section, component, feature, or state inside an established surface inherits that surface. Never turn a local addition into a new identity exercise.

## 2. Ask what will change the work

Ask one round of two or three related questions through the structured question tool when available. Skip settled facts; a precise request may need only a compact confirmation.

- **Persuade:** who must act, what they should believe, which real proof, content, or assets earn that belief.
- **Operate:** the task, information, important states, frequency, constraints.
- **Read:** the reader's question, source material, structure, wayfinding.
- **Experience:** what leads, how exploration unfolds, which interaction or transition matters.

Across modes, ask what success looks like, what must remain untouched, and what would make a polished result feel wrong. Never ask for CSS values or canned aesthetic lanes.

## 3. Choose the right amount of invention

### Extend an existing surface

Inherit its world and composition. Resolve only the new purpose, content, hierarchy, states, interaction, and how the addition joins the surrounding experience. No concept tournament, and no DESIGN.md change unless the user approves a durable system change.

### Create a whole surface inside an established world

Keep the visual system fixed. Derive five to seven materially different structures from the content, task, and user behavior, ordered by resonance. For a genuinely open whole page, screen, or flow, run:

`node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/concept-seed.mjs --scope surface --mode <mode>`

## 4. Commit the world

Pick a color strategy before picking colors: Restrained (neutrals plus one accent; the default when the visitor came to operate or read), Committed (one saturated color carries 30-60% of the surface), Full palette (3-4 named roles), or Drenched (the surface IS the color). Persuade and Experience surfaces have permission for the bolder strategies; take them when the brief allows. Color commits at page scale: fields that own whole regions, not accents scattered over a neutral ground. Dark or light is never a default: write one sentence of physical scene (who uses this, where, under what light) and let it force the answer.

Choose faces like objects from the subject's world, in the mode's register. Operate and Read surfaces are well served by system stacks and workhorse UI faces; Persuade and Experience surfaces want faces with a point of view, and these training-data defaults mean you stopped looking: Fraunces, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Lora, Crimson, Newsreader, Syne, Space Grotesk, Space Mono, IBM Plex, Inter-as-display, DM Sans, DM Serif, Outfit, Plus Jakarta Sans, Instrument Sans. Naming one of these faces anyway requires a reason no other face could satisfy, and a subject association is never that reason: books wanting a serif, bookshops wanting hand-lettering, and tech wanting a mono are the associations the list exists to break.

All are legitimate when the brief calls for them. A direction contract is durable route or artifact strategy, so create or update the brief even when no other surface strategy needs persistence. Keep the contract to six short blocks and 150 words at most. THESIS: the one idea this surface owns and the category-default arrangement it refuses. OWN-WORLD: the palette and component language, specific enough to be recognizable with all content removed. STORY: what the visitor understands, believes, and does. FIRST VIEWPORT: the exact composition, what is where and at what scale, and where the primary action sits. FORM: the chosen form, its position on your ordered list, and the seed key the script printed. Close with one more line, FINISH: the run's exit condition, verbatim "unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance". A compiler or optimizer removing development metadata is not a safety boundary. Reviewers and documenters receive the contract from the surface brief.

import gzip
import io
import tarfile
import unittest
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch
from uuid import uuid4

import httpx
from fastapi import HTTPException
from agentforge.contracts.tasks import TaskCreate
from agentforge.integrations.github_client import GitHubClient, GitHubError, unpack_archive, ResolvedRepository
from agentforge.api.routes_tasks import create_task
from agentforge.repositories.tasks import TaskNotFound

SHA = "a" * 40


def archive(entries):
    raw = io.BytesIO()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="w") as tar:
        for name, data, kind in entries:
            member = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
            member.type = kind
            member.size = len(data) if kind == tarfile.REGTYPE else 0
            member.linkname = "../../outside" if kind in (tarfile.SYMTYPE, tarfile.LNKTYPE) else ""
            tar.addfile(member, io.BytesIO(data) if kind == tarfile.REGTYPE else None)
    return gzip.compress(raw.getvalue())


class ArchiveTests(unittest.TestCase):

        value = unpack_archive(archive([("repo-sha/app.py", b"print('hi')\n", tarfile.REGTYPE),
            ("repo-sha/image.png", b"\x89PNG\0\xff", tarfile.REGTYPE)]))
        self.assertEqual(value["image.png"], b"\x89PNG\0\xff")
        self.assertEqual(set(value), {"app.py", "image.png"})

    def test_unsafe_archives_fail_as_a_whole(self):
        cases = [("root/../outside", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/link", tarfile.SYMTYPE),
            ("root/link", tarfile.LNKTYPE), ("root/fifo", tarfile.FIFOTYPE),
            ("root/.git/config", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/.env.local", tarfile.REGTYPE),
            ("root/.ssh/config", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/a\\b", tarfile.REGTYPE)]
        for name, kind in cases:
            with self.subTest(name=name, kind=kind), self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
                unpack_archive(archive([("root/ok", b"ok", tarfile.REGTYPE), (name, b"bad", kind)]))

    def test_collisions_and_limits_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            unpack_archive(archive([("root/A", b"1", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/a", b"2", tarfile.REGTYPE)]))
        with self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            unpack_archive(archive([("root/file", b"x" * 1_000_001, tarfile.REGTYPE)]))
        with self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            unpack_archive(archive([("root/a", b"1", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/a/b", b"2", tarfile.REGTYPE)]))
        with patch("agentforge.integrations.github_client.MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES", 1000), self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            unpack_archive(gzip.compress(b"x" * 1001))
        with patch("agentforge.integrations.github_client.MAX_FILES", 1), self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            unpack_archive(archive([("root/a", b"1", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/b", b"2", tarfile.REGTYPE)]))

                return httpx.Response(200, content=archive([("repo-sha/a", b"abc", tarfile.REGTYPE)]))
            if "/commits/" in request.url.path:
                return httpx.Response(200, json={"sha": SHA})
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"private": False, "full_name": "owner/repo", "default_branch": "main"})
        result = await GitHubClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(respond)).snapshot("owner/repo", SHA)
        self.assertEqual(result.files, {"a": b"abc"})
        self.assertEqual(result.commit_sha, SHA)
        self.assertTrue(all("authorization" not in request.headers and "cookie" not in request.headers for request in seen))
        self.assertEqual({request.url.host for request in seen}, {"api.github.com", "codeload.github.com"})

    async def test_private_redirect_and_invalid_slug_rejected(self):
        for status, payload in [(200, {"private": True}), (302, {})]:
            requests = []
            def respond(request):
                requests.append(request)
                return httpx.Response(status, json=payload, headers={"location": "https://evil.invalid"})
            with self.subTest(status=status), self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
                await GitHubClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(respond)).resolve("owner/repo", "main")
            self.assertEqual(len(requests), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            await GitHubClient().resolve("../repo", "main")
        with self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
            await GitHubClient().snapshot("owner/repo", "main")

    async def test_issue_actual_content(self):
        def respond(request):
            if "/issues/" in request.url.path:
                return httpx.Response(200, json={"number": 12, "title": "Fix", "body": "Expected behavior", "state": "open"})
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"private": False})
        issue = await GitHubClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(respond)).get_issue("owner/repo", 12)
        self.assertEqual(issue["body"], "Expected behavior")
        self.assertEqual(issue["url"], "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/12")

    def body(self, **changes):
        return TaskCreate(project_id=uuid4(), goal="Implement a bounded test change", kind="coding", coding={
            "repository": {"repo_id": "owner/repo", "ref": "main"}, "test_profiles": ["python_unittest"]}, **changes)

    async def test_owner_is_checked_before_github_and_pin_before_queue(self):
        owner = uuid4()
        repository = SimpleNamespace(authorize_project=lambda **kw: None, create=lambda **kw: kw)
        with patch("agentforge.api.routes_tasks.GitHubClient.resolve", AsyncMock(return_value=ResolvedRepository("owner/repo", SHA, "main"))):
            result = await create_task(self.body(), self.request(), SimpleNamespace(id=owner), repository)
        self.assertEqual(result["owner_id"], owner)
        self.assertEqual(result["request"].coding.repository.ref, SHA)
        def deny(**kw):
            raise TaskNotFound()
        repository.authorize_project = deny
        with patch("agentforge.api.routes_tasks.GitHubClient.resolve", AsyncMock()) as github:
            with self.assertRaises(HTTPException) as error:
                await create_task(self.body(), self.request(), SimpleNamespace(id=owner), repository)
            self.assertEqual(error.exception.status_code, 404)
            github.assert_not_called()

    async def test_missing_sandbox_does_not_queue(self):
        request = self.request()
        request.app.state.settings.e2b_api_key = None
        create = unittest.mock.Mock()
        repository = SimpleNamespace(authorize_project=lambda **kw: None, create=create)
        with self.assertRaises(HTTPException) as error:
            await create_task(self.body(), request, SimpleNamespace(id=uuid4()), repository)
        self.assertEqual(error.exception.status_code, 503)
        create.assert_not_called()

    def test_research_default_remains_compatible_and_identity_is_forbidden(self):
        body = TaskCreate(project_id=uuid4(), goal="Research bounded evidence sources")
        self.assertEqual(body.kind, "research")
        self.assertIsNone(body.coding)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            TaskCreate(project_id=uuid4(), goal=body.goal, created_by=uuid4())
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            TaskCreate(project_id=uuid4(), goal=body.goal, kind="coding")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def archive(entries):
    raw = io.BytesIO()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="w") as tar:
        for name, data, kind in entries:
            member = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
            member.type = kind
            member.size = len(data) if kind == tarfile.REGTYPE else 0
            member.linkname = "../../outside" if kind in (tarfile.SYMTYPE, tarfile.LNKTYPE) else ""
            tar.addfile(member, io.BytesIO(data) if kind == tarfile.REGTYPE else None)
    return gzip.compress(raw.getvalue())

        self.assertEqual(value["image.png"], b"\x89PNG\0\xff")
        self.assertEqual(set(value), {"app.py", "image.png"})

        cases = [("root/../outside", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/link", tarfile.SYMTYPE),
            ("root/link", tarfile.LNKTYPE), ("root/fifo", tarfile.FIFOTYPE),
            ("root/.git/config", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/.env.local", tarfile.REGTYPE),
            ("root/.ssh/config", tarfile.REGTYPE), ("root/a\\b", tarfile.REGTYPE)]
        for name, kind in cases:
            with self.subTest(name=name, kind=kind), self.assertRaises(GitHubError):
                unpack_archive(archive([("root/ok", b"ok", tarfile.REGTYPE), (name, b"bad", kind)]))

"""Bind capability templates to concrete, server-authorized task resources."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import UUID

from agentforge.contracts.agent_definition import AgentDefinition, Budget, Permissions, TOOL_CAPABILITIES, ToolName


class ScopeDenied(PermissionError):
    """A capability or a referenced resource is outside the current task."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskContext:
    """Internal service context; never deserialize this from model/tool arguments.

    Resource sets in every grant ceiling must be concrete. Context references
    are opaque immutable IDs validated by the application's resource resolver.
    """

    user_id: UUID
    project_id: UUID
    task_id: UUID
    platform_permissions: Permissions
    user_permissions: Permissions
    task_permissions: Permissions
    parent_permissions: Permissions
    platform_budget: Budget
    tier_budget: Budget
    task_budget: Budget
    parent_budget: Budget
    authorized_context_refs: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    depth: int = 0
    source_discovery_enabled: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EffectiveScope:
    permissions: Permissions
    allowed_tools: tuple[ToolName, ...]
    budget: Budget
    context_refs: tuple[str, ...]


def intersect_and_validate(
    definition: AgentDefinition, ctx: TaskContext, context_refs: tuple[str, ...],
) -> EffectiveScope:
    if ctx.depth != 0:
        raise ScopeDenied("nested sub-agent delegation is disabled")
    # Round-trip through JSON revalidates even models constructed with model_copy.
    definition = AgentDefinition.model_validate_json(definition.model_dump_json())
    ceilings = [Permissions.model_validate_json(p.model_dump_json()) for p in (
        ctx.platform_permissions, ctx.user_permissions, ctx.task_permissions, ctx.parent_permissions,
    )]
    values: dict[str, object] = {}
    for name in Permissions.model_fields:
        if name.startswith("allowed_"):
            grants = [getattr(p, name) for p in ceilings]
            if any(grant is None for grant in grants):
                raise ScopeDenied(f"missing concrete authorization ceiling: {name}")
            resource_set = set(grants[0])
            for grant in grants[1:]:
                resource_set.intersection_update(grant)
            requested = getattr(definition.permissions, name)
            if requested is not None:
                resource_set.intersection_update(requested)
            values[name] = tuple(sorted(resource_set))
        else:
            values[name] = all(getattr(p, name) for p in [*ceilings, definition.permissions])
    permissions = Permissions.model_validate(values)
    references = set(context_refs)
    if not references.issubset(ctx.authorized_context_refs) or not references.issubset(permissions.allowed_context_refs or ()):
        raise ScopeDenied("context reference is not authorized for this task")
    if len(references) != len(context_refs):
        raise ScopeDenied("duplicate context references")
    budgets = [Budget.model_validate_json(b.model_dump_json()) for b in (
        ctx.platform_budget, ctx.tier_budget, ctx.task_budget, ctx.parent_budget, definition.budget,
    )]
    budget = Budget.model_validate({name: min(getattr(b, name) for b in budgets) for name in Budget.model_fields})
    tools = tuple(tool for tool in definition.allowed_tools if all(
        getattr(permissions, flag) for flag in TOOL_CAPABILITIES[tool]
    ))
    if not tools:
        raise ScopeDenied("no tools remain within the authorized grant intersection")
    return EffectiveScope(permissions, tools, budget, context_refs)

"""Pinned imported repository reads; no Git process or host checkout."""
import hashlib
from decimal import Decimal
from agentforge.sandbox.workspace import read_text
from .contracts import ToolOutcome


def register_repository_read(catalog, repository, github):
    async def read(args, execution):
        files = repository.files(execution.task, baseline=True)
        data = files[args.path]
        try:
            text = read_text(files, args.path)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError("binary_file_not_readable_as_text") from None
        state = repository.session(execution.task)
        payload = dict(path=args.path, sha256=hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), byte_size=len(data),
            line_count=len(text.splitlines()) if text is not None else None, binary=text is None)
        saved = repository.record_evidence(execution.task, operation_key=execution.operation_key,
            kind="repository_read", revision=state["revision"], payload=payload)
        return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data={**payload, "content": text[:10000] if text is not None else None,
            "truncated": text is not None and len(text) > 10000},
            evidence_ids=(saved["evidence_id"],), cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    async def listing(args, execution):
        files = repository.files(execution.task, baseline=True)
        prefix = "" if args.path == "." else args.path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        paths = [path for path in files if path.startswith(prefix)]
        preview = []
        size = 0
        for path in paths:
            size += len(path.encode()) + 4
            if size > 10000:
                break
            preview.append(path)
        return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data={"paths": preview, "truncated": len(paths) > len(preview)}, cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    async def search(args, execution):
        files = repository.files(execution.task, baseline=True)
        matches = []
        for path in files:
            try:
                text = read_text(files, path)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
                if args.query.casefold() in line.casefold():
                    matches.append(dict(path=path, line=number, text=line[:300]))
                    if len(matches) >= 30:
                        break
            if len(matches) >= 30:
                break
        state = repository.session(execution.task)
        saved = repository.record_evidence(execution.task, operation_key=execution.operation_key,
            kind="repository_search", revision=state["revision"], payload={"matches": matches})
        return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data={"matches": matches}, evidence_ids=(saved["evidence_id"],), cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    async def issue(args, execution):
        value = await github.get_issue(args.repo_id, args.issue_number)
        state = repository.session(execution.task)
        saved = repository.record_evidence(execution.task, operation_key=execution.operation_key,
            kind="repository_issue", revision=state["revision"], payload=value)
        return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data=value, evidence_ids=(saved["evidence_id"],), cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    for name, handler in (("read_repo_file", read), ("list_repo_files", listing), ("search_repo", search), ("get_issue", issue)):
        catalog.register(name, handler, max_cost_usd=Decimal(0))

def register_sandbox_files(catalog, repository):
    async def read(args, execution):
        files = repository.files(execution.task)
        text = read_text(files, args.path)
        state = repository.session(execution.task)
        saved = repository.record_evidence(execution.task, operation_key=execution.operation_key,
            kind="workspace_read", revision=state["revision"], payload=dict(path=args.path,
                sha256=hashlib.sha256(files[args.path]).hexdigest()))
        return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data=dict(path=args.path, content=text[:10000],

            revision=state["revision"]), evidence_ids=(saved["evidence_id"],), cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    async def write(args, execution):
        value = repository.write_file(execution.task, operation_key=execution.operation_key,
            path=args.path, content=args.content, expected_sha256=args.expected_sha256)
        return ToolOutcome(status="ok", data=value, cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    async def diff(args, execution):
        changed, data = repository.diff(execution.task)
        state = repository.session(execution.task)

            changed_paths=changed, revision=state["revision"], truncated=len(data) > 10000),
            evidence_ids=(saved["evidence_id"],), artifact_ids=(saved["artifact_id"],), cost_usd=Decimal(0))

    for name, handler in (("read_sandbox_file", read), ("write_sandbox_file", write), ("git_diff", diff)):
        catalog.register(name, handler, max_cost_usd=Decimal(0))

class FetchWebpageArgs(ToolArguments):
    source_url: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=2048)


class RepoArgs(ToolArguments):
    repo_id: ResourceId


class RepoFileArgs(RepoArgs):
    ref: Ref
    path: Path


class RepoSearchArgs(RepoArgs):
    ref: Ref
    query: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)

    ref: Ref
    path: Path = "."


class IssueArgs(RepoArgs):
    issue_number: int = Field(ge=1)


class PRStatusArgs(RepoArgs):
    pr_number: int = Field(ge=1)


class SandboxArgs(ToolArguments):
    sandbox_id: ResourceId


class SandboxFileArgs(SandboxArgs):
    path: Path


class SandboxWriteArgs(SandboxFileArgs):
    content: str = Field(max_length=100_000)
    # Future sandbox adapters must compare this hash before a write.
    expected_sha256: str | None = Field(default=None, pattern=r"^[a-f0-9]{64}$")


class GitDiffArgs(SandboxArgs):
    base_ref: Ref


class SandboxCommandArgs(SandboxArgs):
    command_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64, pattern=r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_\-]+$")
    args: Annotated[tuple[Annotated[str, Field(max_length=512)], ...], Field(strict=False, max_length=20)] = ()


class RunTestsArgs(SandboxArgs):
    test_profile: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64, pattern=r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_\-]+$")


class TestResultsArgs(ToolArguments):
    task_id: ResourceId
    run_id: ResourceId


class BrowserArgs(ToolArguments):
    url: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=2048)
    checks: Annotated[tuple[Literal["title", "screenshot", "links", "accessibility"], ...], Field(strict=False, max_length=4)] = ("title",)

    "web_search": WebSearchArgs, "fetch_webpage": FetchWebpageArgs,
    "read_repo_file": RepoFileArgs, "search_repo": RepoSearchArgs,
    "get_issue": IssueArgs, "list_repo_files": RepoFilesArgs,
    "read_sandbox_file": SandboxFileArgs, "write_sandbox_file": SandboxWriteArgs,
    "git_diff": GitDiffArgs, "run_sandbox_command": SandboxCommandArgs,
    "run_tests": RunTestsArgs, "get_test_results": TestResultsArgs,
    "get_pr_status": PRStatusArgs, "browser_public_page": BrowserArgs,
}


class ToolOutcome(BaseModel):
    """Adapter output. IDs require independent task ownership verification."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, allow_inf_nan=False)
    status: Literal["ok", "error"]
    data: dict[str, JsonValue] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    evidence_ids: tuple[ResourceId, ...] = ()
    artifact_ids: tuple[ResourceId, ...] = ()
    # None means the remote charge is unknown, retaining the operation cap.
    cost_usd: Decimal | None
    error_code: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=64, pattern=r"^[A-Z_]+$")

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def bounded(self) -> Self:
        if self.cost_usd is not None and (not self.cost_usd.is_finite() or self.cost_usd < 0):
            raise ValueError("invalid tool cost")
        if self.status == "error" and self.error_code is None:
            raise ValueError("tool errors require a safe code")
        if len(self.evidence_ids) > 100 or len(self.artifact_ids) > 100:
            raise ValueError("too many result references")
        if len(json.dumps(self.model_dump(mode="json"), allow_nan=False).encode()) > 262144:
            raise ValueError("tool result exceeds bounded storage limit")
        return self


# Every request variant has its own argument schema; arbitrary tool names do not
# become executable merely because a provider emits them.
class _Request(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)


class WebSearchRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["web_search"]
    args: WebSearchArgs


class FetchRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["fetch_webpage"]
    args: FetchWebpageArgs


class RepoFileRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["read_repo_file"]
    args: RepoFileArgs


class RepoSearchRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["search_repo"]
    args: RepoSearchArgs


class IssueRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["get_issue"]
    args: IssueArgs


class RepoFilesRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["list_repo_files"]
    args: RepoFilesArgs


class SandboxFileRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["read_sandbox_file"]
    args: SandboxFileArgs


class SandboxWriteRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["write_sandbox_file"]
    args: SandboxWriteArgs


class DiffRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["git_diff"]
    args: GitDiffArgs


class CommandRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["run_sandbox_command"]
    args: SandboxCommandArgs


class TestsRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["run_tests"]
    args: RunTestsArgs


class TestResultsRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["get_test_results"]
    args: TestResultsArgs


class PRStatusRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["get_pr_status"]
    args: PRStatusArgs


class BrowserRequest(_Request):
    name: Literal["browser_public_page"]
    args: BrowserArgs

    IssueRequest | RepoFilesRequest | SandboxFileRequest | SandboxWriteRequest |
    DiffRequest | CommandRequest | TestsRequest | TestResultsRequest |
    PRStatusRequest | BrowserRequest,
    Field(discriminator="name"),
]
